reason: The cited evidence does not directly address the NbZrTiHfMo system, the role of electronegativity difference, or the specific effects of Nb substitution on plasticity and strength in this alloy. E1 provides general background on RHEAs, and E2 discusses property trends in a different alloy system (HfMoNbTaTiZr) without supporting the key mechanistic claims.
premises: High Mo content increases electronegativity difference and is associated with reduced plasticity in NbZrTiHfMo.
Nb is a ductile element that can improve plasticity when substituted for Mo.
Reducing Mo content by Nb substitution will reduce the electronegativity difference in the BCC matrix.
Solid solution strengthening from Mo can be largely preserved after partial Nb substitution, maintaining high yield strength.
The BCC phase will remain stable under the proposed compositional adjustment.
